location: Queanbeyan, Capital Region / Southern Tablelands, NSW, Australia

main_turf.surface: Turf (Couch grass on clay loam base)
main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). Premier country circuit in the NSW Capital Region bordering the ACT. Features a tight 1,460m 'bullring' oval layout with a very short 240m home straight. Due to the tight turns and brief home stretch, early speed ('E' style) and rail-running pressers ('P' style) hold a heavy advantage. Off-pace swoopers ('C' style) face severe penalties unless an extreme front-end pace battle occurs.
main_turf.post_bias: STRONG INSIDE BARRIER ADVANTAGE: Inside barrier draws (1-4) are critical over 900m, 1000m, and 1200m sprints. Tight turns into the short 240m home straight make wide draws (7+) exceptionally penalizing as runners get forced wide.

handicapping_angles.tight_bullring_240m_straight_speed_lock: Queanbeyan's 240m home straight is one of the shortest in NSW. Early leaders ('E' style) with 'is_lone_speed': true that lead around the home turn are almost impossible to run down. Grant a strong early speed upgrade (+4.0 pts).
handicapping_angles.canberra_act_shipper_advantage: Located adjacent to the ACT, Queanbeyan receives high-volume entries from Canberra-based trainers (e.g. Keith Dryden, Matthew Dale, Gratz Vella, Joseph & Jones, Nick Olive). Canberra provincial form carries a distinct class and speed figure advantage over regional country rivals (+3.0 pts class angle).
handicapping_angles.cutaway_rail_inside_sprint_lane: Queanbeyan frequently utilizes a cutaway rail entering the 240m home straight. Horses box-seating behind the leader along the inside rail receive an instant sprint lane without having to fan wide around turns.
handicapping_angles.queanbeyan_cup_feature: The Queanbeyan Cup ($50k+ Country Showcase Handicap, October) is the feature event of the Queanbeyan season. Upgrade horses with proven Canberra or Kembla Grange benchmark form.
